stem_book: When a man moves down the inclined plane with a constant speed 5 ms⁻¹ which makes an angle of 37° with the horizontal, he finds that the rain is falling vertically downward. When he moves up the same inclined plane with the same speed, he finds that the rain makes an angle θ = tan⁻¹(7/8) with the horizontal. The speed of the rain is: (a) √116 ms⁻¹ (b) √32 ms⁻¹ (c) 5 ms⁻¹ (d) √73 ms⁻¹
reason: Manifest said 'rain falls vertically' (true rain direction); print says the rain APPEARS vertical to the man moving down — corrected.
work: v_man(down) = (4, −3): rain rel vertical ⇒ rx = 4; v_man(up) = (−4, 3): rel = (8, ry − 3), tan = 7/8 ⇒ ry = −4 ⇒ |v_rain| = √(16 + 16) = √32
